name: workforceos
description: Timesheets and approvals with PostgreSQL, transactional decisions, audit history, tests and a live demo

paragraphs: A working timesheet and approvals product, built as a full-stack engineering case study.

WorkforceOS models a small but real operational workflow: employees record time, submit it, and a manager approves or rejects it. The dashboard, queue, and audit log all read from PostgreSQL. Each visitor receives a private demo workspace with synthetic data, so the public demo is safe to explore.
The interesting part of a timesheet system is not the form. It is the consistency of decisions under multiple actors and repeated requests. This repository focuses on the workflow boundary:
features: Role checks on the server: team members can submit only their own entries; only the manager can decide a submitted entry.
Explicit state machine: draft → submitted → approved/rejected, with resubmission after rejection. Invalid transitions fail.
Transactional decisions: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the entry while the status and audit event are written in one transaction. Duplicate decisions cannot both succeed.
Database constraints: valid statuses, hour bounds, and one entry per person, project, and date within a demo workspace.
Private visitor data: an opaque, HTTP-only cookie points to a dedicated workspace. Sample records are fictional.

whatItDoes.text: A working timesheet and approvals product, built as a full-stack engineering case study.

requirements.text: The role checks demonstrate the domain boundary inside one isolated sandbox; a production tenant would add real sign-in, organization membership, authorization middleware, rate limiting, retention policy, and operational monitoring.
